risks: CAUSAL-ONLY EXTRAS ARE INHERENT: the proposal floor is relative (max(0.5, 30% of global peak)), so a weak early movement can be a valid proposal at close time and retro-subthreshold later (measured: rally2 E1 0.60 u/s). The engine flags these (SESSION_EVENT_RETRO_SUPPRESSED) but downstream must decide how to present them — proposal: dispatch analysis anyway, badge the event 'weak relative to session', never delete.

O(n²) reconciliation: proposeStrokeEventsV2 re-runs over the full accumulated series each push — trivial at replay scale (≤134 samples) but a 10-min 30Hz session is ~18k samples; a windowed-lookback variant changes global-peak threshold semantics and MUST be re-validated against this replay harness before use.

Trailing flush: if the user stops mid-swing the last event closes as 'flush' with the best available bounds — correct for user-stop, but Wave B UI should mark flush-closed events as boundary-uncertain.

Theoretical glue divergence (documented in sessionEngine.ts): a fragment starting ≤350ms after a frozen end would have glued into the emitted event in the acausal batch; it becomes its own event or a recorded suppression instead — not observed on either replay run (0 occurrences), watch for it when more continuous footage lands.

n=2 dev runs / 5 events — replay evidence only, no reliability claim; the 2/5 gold completion-bench cases that hit safety-max (D-029) are exactly the continuous-exchange class where the valley primitive matters most, and gold labels for multi-event sessions are still 0 (DATA #1).
